candidate.answerReason: Running the same half-distance at three times the speed takes 2 minutes. Adding the 6 walking minutes gives 8 minutes, matching D.

methods.label: Compare times for equal distances
methods.explanation:
Joe walks half the journey and runs the other half, so the two distances are equal. Covering the same distance at three times the speed takes one-third as much time. His running time is therefore
\[
6\div3=2\text{ minutes}.
\]
Adding the walking and running times gives \(6+2=\boxed{8}\) minutes, choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the elementary inverse relationship between speed and time for a fixed distance.

candidate.annotationRationale: Equal distances make travel time inversely proportional to speed. The distance equals speed times time relationship supports this comparison; direct proportion is not required.

review.mathematicalCheck: The walking and running distances are equal. Tripling speed divides the time by three, so running takes 6÷3=2 minutes and the whole trip takes 8 minutes, choice D.
review.levelCheck: The fixed-distance comparison is elementary, and the explanation states why the time decreases by a factor of three.
review.annotationCheck: Inverse proportion accurately describes the assessed relationship. The distance-speed-time relationship is justified support.
